text: So much of what teams know lives in video: bug reports, meetings, lectures, support calls. Agents read every log and doc. Hand them a video, and they're blind.

Because video is hard. Nearly two thousand frames a minute, with meaning split between what's shown and what's said. One look costs hundreds of thousands of tokens. Answers come without proof. And an agent can't just sign up and pay.
MediaPack fixes all of it. Index a video once, ask anything, and get answers pinned to the second, with proof. Agents pay per use.

Upload a recording. The server verifies the real file and quotes fifty cents. The agent pays for itself with Stripe machine payments: the price arrives as an HTTP four-oh-two. No account. No API key. No checkout.

Then the work travels as email over Primitive. Every job is a real thread: a work order out, and a verified result back from an isolated Blaxel worker running ffmpeg, Whisper and vision. Deduplicated, and retrievable after the job is done.
Watch it live on a sample talk. One question, emailed to a worker, and answered in under ten seconds, pinned to the moment it was said.
On a bug recording, it catches the regression: saved as sixty, shown as thirty after reload. Click the citation and the source jumps there, with every frame and clip hash-verified.
Index once, ask many times. Three hundred twenty-seven thousand tokens to index. About twenty-five hundred per question after that.

Every piece earns its place. Stripe for agent payments. Primitive for an auditable thread per job. Blaxel for isolated runs that scale to zero. Supabase for limits enforced in Postgres. And Manufact, so any agent plugs in over MCP.
MediaPack. Searchable, payable, provable video for agents. Live today, and open source.
